sources.entry: Kumquat - Menu bar file converter: drag files, tap Shift and drop them on a wheel to convert images, audio, video and documents, compress, OCR, trim and annotate. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/TheAlexRay/kumquat) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Petalwheel (formerly Kumquat) is a macOS menu-bar file converter where you drag files, tap Shift, and drop them on a radial wheel to convert, compress, OCR, edit or archive them.
summary.what_it_does: Petalwheel runs from the macOS menu bar. You start dragging files in Finder or another app, tap Shift while holding the mouse, and a wheel opens under the cursor; dropping files on a petal runs the action, with results saved next to the originals. The wheel only offers actions that apply to every dragged file. Conversions cover images, camera RAW, audio, video, documents, spreadsheets, subtitles and archives. Other tools include compression, metadata stripping, loudness normalization, OCR, QR reading, PDF merge/split, collages, and archive creation with AES-256 ZIP passwords. The README also describes interactive editors (Annotate, Redact, Adjust, Organize PDF, Trim, Bleep, Redact Video), folder batch operations, user presets, and a CLI with --convert, --tool and --list options.
use_cases: convert photos between HEIC, JPG, PNG and WebP
compress videos or PDFs to a target size
extract text from scanned images with OCR
batch convert a folder of files
trim video or audio and cut silence
how_to_run: brew install meson ninja cmake pkgconf
notable: Drag-and-drop wheel: tap Shift mid-drag to open a radial menu of actions applicable to the dragged files
No Accessibility permission needed; it polls the mouse, modifier keys and drag pasteboard
Originals are never modified; results are written beside them
Folder mode converts contents into a sibling ' (converted)' folder and can flatten nested folders or report sizes
Bilingual UI (English and Russian) and a CLI with English-only output
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or later
Builds are ad-hoc signed until a Developer ID is set up, so the first launch is blocked by macOS and needs a manual override
Some formats need extra tools, e.g. zstd requires brew install zstd; full bundled build needs a long first-time ffmpeg build
Folder runs are capped at 10,000 files and skip hidden files, app bundles and symlinks
